If you are a freelance artist, publicist or art teacher, you should apply for the Künstlersozialkasse (KSK). This guide explains why and how.

The Künstlersozialkasse (KSK) is a social fund for freelance artists, publicists and art teachers. It’s funded by the government, and by businesses who hire freelance artists. When you are a KSK member, they pay half of your health insurance, long-term care insurance and public pension insurance. There is no membership fee.
Because it’s a really good deal. The Künstlersozialkasse helps you get public health insurance and save for retirement.

title: Advantages
text: They pay half of your health insurance Normally, freelancers pay € 250 to € 1,310 per month for public health insurance. If you are in the KSK, you pay 50% less. You get the same coverage. They pay half of your public pension insurance Public pension insurance is optional for most freelancers, so you probably don’t pay for it. If you join the KSK, it’s required, but the KSK pays half of it. You get a public pension for half the price. It lets you get public health insurance Some freelancers are stuck with private health insurance, or bad expat health insurance. When you join the KSK, you can switch to public health insurance. It’s often the best option for you. It helps you get permanent residence Before you apply for permanent residence, you must pay public pension insurance for 60 months. The KSK makes public pension insurance more affordable for freelancers. You get more things for the same price If you earn less than € 69,750 per year, your net income stays the same. If you earn more, you pay a little more, but it’s still a really good deal.

title: Disadvantages
text: There is a lot of paperwork The KSK application process is a bit hard. It takes a few months to get accepted. You might need to try multiple times. If you don’t speak German, you might need a translator. They reject a lot of people You might need to try multiple times, and still get rejected. Some people give up. Others sue the KSK to get accepted. You can’t always keep your private health insurance If you earn less than € 77,400 per year, you must switch to public health insurance. It’s usually a good thing, but you might prefer to keep your private health insurance. It can limit your options Artistic/journalistic activities must be your main source of income. If you have other sources of income, it can be complicated. You might need to refuse some contracts to stay in the KSK. You can still have a side job and stay in the KSK. Backpayments When the KSK accepts you, your membership starts from the date you applied. If they take 5 months to accept you, you are a member for those 5 months. In some cases, you must make health insurance and pension insurance backpayments for that period.

text: This means that… You work for profit It’s a business, not a hobby. You must charge money for your services. text: This means that… You have many clients You are not working for only one agency, orchestra, theatre group, film production or art school. title: You work in Germany
text: This means that… You work from Germany You must work from Germany at least 25% of the time, even if your clients are in other countries. You don’t need German clients to join the KSK. title: You are not an employer
text: This means that… You have maximum one employee You can only hire one other employee. You can hire as many contractors, freelancers, apprentices, minijob employees as you want.

section: How to apply for the KSK
text: You do not automatically join the KSK. You must apply for it. If you don’t join the KSK, nobody will force you.

section: How to apply for the KSK
title: Is it hard to apply?
text: It’s not that hard. If you clearly meet the requirements, then it’s easy. If your case is not clear, then it’s a bit harder. You must send a lot of documents to prove that you are an artist, publicist or art teacher. This includes a resume, a portfolio, bank statements, letters of reference, reviews, contracts, invoices and more. It takes a few days to gather all the documents. You must do everything in German. If you don’t speak German, you will need a translator. The KSK often asks more questions in German. Staying in the KSK is easy. Once a year, you must tell them your predicted income. Each year, the KSK audits 5% of its members. If this happens to you, you must show tax declarations and other documents from the last 4 years. It’s more work, but it’s not hard.

section: How to apply for the KSK
title: How long does it take?
text: The KSK needs 2 to 4 months to decide, but they can take up to 1 year. If you prepare your application well, the KSK sometimes decides faster. After you fill the registration form, you have 4 weeks to send the required documents. Then the KSK needs 2 to 4 months to make a decision. They often ask more questions, or ask for more documents. Each time, it takes a few weeks. If the KSK rejects you, you must send more documents to appeal their decision. This takes more time.

section: How to apply for the KSK
title: 5. Send everything to the KSK
text: After you fill the registration form, you have 4 weeks to send your documents. There are 2 ways to send your documents: By post Put all your documents in an envelope, and send it by registered mail to Künstlersozialkasse, Gökerstraße 14, 26384 Wilhelmshaven. By De-Mail If you have a De-Mail account, you can use it to send your documents. It’s easier to apply by post, but De-Mail is useful if you are currently travelling, and you can’t receive post. Print all your documents on A4 paper. If you have documents in other sizes, make an A4 photocopy. Do not staple the documents. They will be scanned page by page. Send copies, not the original documents. Do not include books, pamphlets, business cards, CDs, DVDs or USB drives, only A4 documents. If you want to show external websites, print screenshots of them. How to mail a letter — from your computer, without a printer

section: How to apply for the KSK
title: 6. Wait
text: The KSK will answer by post. It takes 3 to 9 months. It took me 3 months to get the first answer, and 7½ months to get the first decision. While you wait, you can send more documents to support your application. Just include your reference number. They will probably ask more questions, or require more documents. Don’t take it personally. You have 1 month to answer. Answer quickly. It shows that you care, and it makes them work faster. You have around 4 weeks to answer before they delete your application. Most KSK applications are rejected because applicants are too slow.

section: How to apply for the KSK
title: 7. Rejected by the KSK?
text: The KSK can reject your application. If this happens, do not give up! The rejection letter from the KSK explains why they refused your application. You have 1 month to oppose their decision. If you are in another country, you have 3 months. You must send the letter by post or De-mail. Emails are not accepted. To oppose the decision, you must write a letter that explains why you qualify for the KSK, and why their refusal is not valid. For example, the KSK rejected me because my income comes from advertising, not selling texts. I cited a court case that shows that this is allowed, and that I have a right to join the KSK. I cited the parts of the court case that apply to my situation.

title: Backpayments
text: Your KSK membership starts on the day you applied, not on the day they accept you. For example, if you apply in February, and the KSK approves your application in October, you are a KSK member since February. This means that after the KSK accepts you, you must make retroactive pension payments for the months you waited. For example, if they take 8 months to accept your application, you must make 8 months of pension insurance backpayments. If you have public health insurance, the KSK also retroactively pays half of your health insurance. What happens depends on which health insurance you had while you waited: If you had public health insurance The KSK refunds half of your health insurance payments since the date you applied. You can keep the same health insurance. If you had private health insurance The KSK sometimes refunds half of your private health insurance payments. You must usually switch to public health insurance one full month after the KSK accepts you. For example, if they accept you at the end of June, you must switch to public health insurance in August. You can sometimes keep your private health insurance. If you had expat health insurance The KSK does not refund half of your expat health insurance payments. You must switch to public health insurance as soon as the KSK accepts you.

title: You pay every month
text: You must pay the KSK every month. There are 2 ways to do it: Automatically with a direct debit authorization. When you apply for the KSK, include this form. This is the easiest way. Manually with a bank transfer.

title: Costs depend on predicted income
text: Every year, you must tell the KSK your predicted income for the next year. The KSK uses your predicted income to calculate your monthly payments. This is called the Jahresmeldung. You do it online. If your predicted income is wrong, it’s okay. If your predicted income is too low, you pay less than you should. The KSK will not ask you to pay more. Good for you. If your predicted income is too high, you pay more than you should. The KSK will not give you any money back. Bad for you. If your prediction is really wrong, then you can make a correction ( Änderungsmitteilung). The KSK will adjust your future payments. They will not ask you to pay more for the past months. They will not give you any money back. If you make bad predictions on purpose, the KSK can fine you up to € 5,000. They can also kick you out. They can’t ask you to pay more for the past months.

title: Random audits
text: Every year, the KSK verifies 5% of its members. They choose at random. If they verify you, you have 4 weeks to send them your tax declarations of the last 4 years. They will check two things: you still meet the KSK requirements you did not lie about your predicted income

title: When you leave Germany
text: If you leave Germany, you can sometimes get your public pension payments back. You only get the part that you paid (9.3% of your income), not the part that the KSK paid. If you can’t get your pension payments back, you will get a German pension when you retire, even if you live in another country. How to get a pension refund How to leave Germany

title: Can I have private health insurance with the KSK?
text: It depends. After you join the KSK, you can keep your private health insurance if… You were self-employed for less than 3 years or you earned more than € 77,400 per year for 3 years in a row. The KSK pays half of your private health insurance. They pay up to 10.6% of your income, or up to € 613 per month. That’s half the cost of public health insurance and long-term care insurance. If your private health insurance costs more than that, you must pay the extra cost alone. Your private health insurance must offer similar coverage to public health insurance. Expat health insurance is not accepted. You must pay the private health insurer yourself. Instead of giving you money for health insurance, the KSK lowers your pension insurance payments.
